system_description.narrative_title: Shifting security dynamics around the Russia–Ukraine war
system_description.narrative_summary: News converge on a single, system-level story: the Russia–Ukraine war is driving a reconfiguration of European and transatlantic security relationships as military strikes, diplomatic initiatives, and domestic politics interact. The system is open — flows of military aid, diplomacy, energy and information (including cyber/space operations) cross borders and are influenced by external inputs (US political shifts, Turkish mediation, Russian hybrid tactics) and produce outputs (attacks, security deals, internal reforms). Feedback loops — strikes prompting diplomacy, political realignments affecting arms deliveries, and sanctions/evasion altering Russia's logistics — create dynamic, sometimes nonlinear responses across the region.
system_description.scope: Actors, processes and assets directly shaping European security around the Russia–Ukraine conflict: sovereign states (Ukraine, Russia, EU members, US, Turkey), security institutions and dialogues, military capabilities (air defences, missiles, satellite and comms systems), critical infrastructure (power grids, oil refineries, transport), arms and logistics flows, and cyber/strategic communications and information operations.
system_description.super_system: Global order and great-power geopolitics (US–Russia–China strategic competition and international institutions that mediate security and economic relations).
adjacent_subsystems: NATO military coordination and force posture
European Union political cohesion and diplomacy
US domestic politics and defence policy cycles
Russian military-logistics, energy exports and hybrid operations (cyber/space)

variables.name: Military capability
variables.description: The aggregate readiness, size and lethality of deployed and available military forces and platforms.

variables.name: Air defence effectiveness
variables.description: The probability that active and passive air-defence systems will detect, track and neutralize airborne threats.

variables.name: Arms and munitions flow
variables.description: The rate and continuity of delivered weapons, munitions and related materiel crossing borders and supply chains.

variables.name: Logistics resilience
variables.description: The ability of transport, storage and repair networks to sustain military and civilian supply needs under stress.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure resilience
variables.description: The capacity of power, transport and industrial assets to absorb, recover from and continue functioning after attacks or outages.

variables.name: Energy supply stability
variables.description: The steadiness and predictability of fuel and electricity availability for civilian and military use across the region.

variables.name: Cyber operations intensity
variables.description: The frequency, scale and sophistication of offensive and defensive cyber actions affecting networks and services.

variables.name: Information influence pressure
variables.description: The magnitude of coordinated information, media and messaging efforts intended to shape public opinion and decision‑making.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement level
variables.description: The intensity and continuity of formal and informal diplomatic interactions, negotiations and security dialogues.

variables.name: Transatlantic cohesion
variables.description: The degree of policy alignment, burden‑sharing and coordinated action among allied and partner actors across the region.

variables.name: Domestic political stability
variables.description: The steadiness of governing coalitions, public support and institutional functioning within affected polities.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement intensity
variables.description: The vigour, coverage and consistency of measures to restrict economic and financial flows and the capacity to detect evasion.

variables.name: Military communications capacity
variables.description: The availability, redundancy and security of command, control and tactical communications systems for operational use.

variables.name: Space and satellite vulnerability
variables.description: The exposure of space-based sensors, communications and navigation assets to attack, interference or degradation.

variables.name: Population displacement flow
variables.description: The rate and scale of civilian movement and displacement driven by security threats and infrastructure disruption.

variables.name: Deterrence perception
variables.description: The prevailing belief among actors about the credibility and effectiveness of punitive or defensive responses to aggression.
